title: Add Rust RAG offline plugin starter and local testing harness
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a Rust-based RAG offline plugin quickstart with local harness, Dockerfile for reproducible builds, and GitHub Actions smoke tests. Intended as a lightweight starter for teams integrating Rust tooling into RAG authoring pipelines.
description:
Motivation: provide a minimal, production-minded Rust starter for RAG-style workflows that need an offline embedding/index plugin and a reproducible local test harness. Many teams ask for non-Node/Go examples; this quickstart demonstrates a compact Rust crate that (1) loads a static, incremental index (JSONL), (2) exposes a small local HTTP shim for tool-calling, and (3) includes instructions to validate end-to-end behavior against Redwood local emulators. This PR adds the quickstart, docs, CI smoke tests, and a sample index generator.

What changed: single-folder quickstart at quickstarts/rust-rag-offline-plugin with README, example index, Rust crate sources (Cargo.toml, src/main.rs), lightweight Dockerfile for reproducing builds, a helper script scripts/build_wasm.sh (optional wasm target), and .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml to run build+smoke integration. The README includes a short migration note for teams that expect KMS/HSM keys (this starter assumes no external secrets).

Checklist (what I verified):
- [x] Basic crate builds on Linux/macOS with stable toolchain
- [x] Docker image builds and runs the local shim
- [x] Example flow: load index -> query -> retrieve top-n -> call Rust tool -> return structured JSON to caller
- [x] GitHub Actions smoke job that runs the example end-to-end against a lightweight in-memory index
- [x] Documentation with code snippets and troubleshooting tips

Commits summary: 3 commits —
- feat(rust-quickstart): initial scaffold and example index generator
- feat(rust-quickstart): add HTTP shim, retrieval logic, and README
- ci(quickstart): add GH Actions smoke test and Dockerfile

Files touched: quickstarts/rust-rag-offline-plugin/README.md, quickstarts/rust-rag-offline-plugin/Cargo.toml, quickstarts/rust-rag-offline-plugin/src/main.rs, quickstarts/rust-rag-offline-plugin/Dockerfile, quickstarts/rust-rag-offline-plugin/examples/example_index.jsonl, quickstarts/rust-rag-offline-plugin/scripts/build_wasm.sh, .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml, .gitignore

How to run locally (short):
1) git clone && cd quickstarts/rust-rag-offline-plugin
2) cargo build --release
3) cargo run --release -- --index examples/example_index.jsonl --port 4207
4) curl -X POST http://localhost:4207/query -d '{"q":"what is redwood inference?","top_n":3}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
The service responds with a structured JSON object containing retrieved passages and a scored alignment. The README has copies of the sample requests and expected responses.

Compatibility notes: the starter is intentionally minimal (no async runtime-heavy dependencies) to keep binary size small and to be easy to embed in CI. A helper wasm build is included (scripts/build_wasm.sh) showing how a small subset of the logic can be compiled to wasm for edge prototypes. For production inference pipelines, we recommend teams replace the example index loader with their embedding service and wire the retrieval step into Redwood SDK calls.

Security and data handling: this quickstart treats the index as static JSONL and performs no networked model requests. It includes guidance on adding TLS and secrets management in the README if teams transition to servered embeddings or private deployments.

Related: ENG-9123 (cross-language example gaps), PM-204 (docs quickstart initiative).
commit_summary: initial scaffold: add crate, example index generator, and README stub
add retrieval HTTP shim, retrieval ranking, structured responses, and doc examples
add Dockerfile and GitHub Actions smoke test for quickstart
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can we add a short note in the README about expected index schema (field names and types)? Also please verify behavior when top_n > index size.
Maya Chen: Added a dedicated 'index-schema' subsection and tests for small indexes; behavior now returns as many items as available and documents it in README.
Sofia Martinez: CI job failed initially on mac runners due to missing openssl dev headers; suggested using rustls or pinning a pure-Rust dependency. I suggested switch to rustls to avoid native deps.
Maya Chen: Reworked dependency to use rustls and updated Dockerfile; re-ran CI and it passed.
Ethan Gray: Quicknote — add a tiny migration paragraph about secrets if folks swap example loader for customer embeddings. Approved after doc addition.
merge_commit_message:
squash: add rust rag offline plugin starter with local harness and smoke tests

Quickstart that demonstrates an offline Rust plugin for retrieval and a reproducible test harness.
example_run_snippet:
# Build and run the example
cargo build --release && cargo run --release -- --index examples/example_index.jsonl --port 4207
# Query the running shim
curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4207/query -d '{"q":"summarize redwood inference thesis", "top_n":2}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
